statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the 83 plasmid taxonomic units (PTUs) found in the order Enterobacterales, 28 match plasmid archetypes that had been described before.
statements.evidence: We identify 83 PTUs in the order Enterobacterales, 28 of them corresponding to previously described archetypes.
statements.note: The abstract reports 83 PTUs in Enterobacterales, 28 of which correspond to previously described archetypes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: More than three-fifths of the plasmids in the global map belong to groups whose host range extends beyond a single species.
statements.evidence: More than 60% of the plasmids in the global map are in groups with host ranges beyond the species barrier.
statements.note: The abstract states that over 60% of plasmids in the global map sit in groups whose host ranges cross the species barrier.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Plasmid taxonomic units with the broadest host range (grade VI) carry more antibiotic resistance genes than units confined to a single host species (grade I).
statements.evidence: Plasmids can mediate horizontal gene transfer of antibiotic resistance, virulence genes, and other adaptive factors across bacterial populations.
statements.note: Antibiotic resistance appears only as background on what plasmids can transfer; the abstract never links resistance-gene content to PTU host-range grade.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Run across the whole bacterial domain, the automated PTU-identification algorithm found 276 plasmid taxonomic units in total.
statements.evidence: The algorithm reveals a total of 276 PTUs in the bacterial domain.
statements.note: The abstract reports that the automated algorithm reveals 276 PTUs across the bacterial domain.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Homoeolog expression divergence is greater in Pima cotton than in Upland cotton.
statements.evidence: These differential evolutionary trajectories are accompanied by gene-family diversification and homoeolog expression divergence among polyploid lineages.
statements.note: The abstract reports homoeolog expression divergence among polyploid lineages but never compares its extent between Pima and Upland cottons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Two cultivated cottons show parallel similarities in fiber gene expression, a pattern driven by selection and domestication.
statements.evidence: Selection and domestication drive parallel gene expression similarities in fibers of two cultivated cottons
statements.note: The abstract states that selection and domestication drive parallel gene expression similarities in fibers of two cultivated cottons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Polyploidy suppresses recombination in cotton, a suppression that wild introgression is able to overcome.
statements.evidence: polyploidy induces recombination suppression, which correlates with altered epigenetic landscapes and can be overcome by wild introgression
statements.note: The abstract states that polyploidy induces recombination suppression and that wild introgression can overcome it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Gene content and synteny are conserved across the allopolyploid cotton genomes, even though transposon exchanges between subgenomes have diversified them.
statements.evidence: Although these polyploid genomes are conserved in gene content and synteny, they have diversified by subgenomic transposon exchanges
statements.note: The abstract describes the polyploid cotton genomes as conserved in gene content and synteny but diversified by subgenomic transposon exchanges.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The expanded nuclear tree confirms many relationships predicted in earlier work but substantially revises key groups, most of all the rosids.
statements.evidence: provides a critical test of earlier results and brings notable change to key groups, especially in rosids, while substantiating many previously predicted relationships
statements.note: The abstract says the 15-fold larger sampling brings notable change to key groups, especially rosids, while substantiating many previously predicted relationships.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: More than four-fifths of today's angiosperm orders arose during an early phase of explosive diversification marked by high gene tree conflict.
statements.evidence: we discovered that early angiosperm evolution was characterized by high gene tree conflict and explosive diversification, giving rise to more than 80% of extant angiosperm orders
statements.note: The abstract reports that early angiosperm evolution, with high gene tree conflict and explosive diversification, gave rise to more than 80% of extant orders.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After a phase of steady diversification through the rest of the Mesozoic, angiosperm diversification rates increased again in the Cenozoic as global temperatures decreased.
statements.evidence: Steady diversification ensued through the remaining Mesozoic Era until rates resurged in the Cenozoic Era, concurrent with decreasing global temperatures
statements.note: The abstract describes steady Mesozoic diversification followed by a Cenozoic resurgence in rates, concurrent with decreasing global temperatures.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Plastid genomes evolve too slowly to resolve relationships between closely related angiosperm genera.
statements.evidence: However, the limited and biased sampling of both taxa and genomes undermines confidence in the tree and its implications.
statements.note: The abstract blames earlier uncertainty on limited and biased sampling of taxa and genomes and says nothing about how fast plastid genomes evolve.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The two major independent origins of specialized beetle herbivory each line up in time with the first appearance of plant cell wall-degrading enzyme (PCWDE) genes in beetle genomes.
statements.evidence: both major independent origins of specialized herbivory in beetles coincide with the first appearances of an arsenal of PCWDEs encoded in their genomes
statements.note: The abstract states that both major independent origins of specialized herbivory coincide with the first appearances of PCWDEs encoded in beetle genomes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Beetle lineages that carry plant cell wall-degrading enzyme (PCWDE) genes have lower extinction rates than beetle lineages lacking them.
statements.evidence: Beetle diversity thus appears to have resulted from multiple factors, including low extinction rates over a long evolutionary history
statements.note: Low extinction rates are cited only as one general factor in beetle diversity; the abstract never compares extinction between lineages with and without PCWDE genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The phylogenomic analyses place the beginning of the beetle lineage in the Carboniferous and support codiversification of beetles with angiosperms.
statements.evidence: Phylogenomic analyses of these uniquely comprehensive datasets resolved previously controversial beetle relationships, dated the origin of Coleoptera to the Carboniferous, and supported the codiversification of beetles and angiosperms.
statements.note: The abstract reports that the phylogenomic analyses dated Coleoptera to the Carboniferous and supported beetle-angiosperm codiversification.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Beetle diversification rates increased during the Jurassic, at times corresponding to the origins of specialized herbivory.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, corresponding (Jurassic) diversification rate increases suggest that these novel genes triggered adaptive radiations
statements.note: The abstract reports corresponding Jurassic diversification rate increases; only the idea that the new genes triggered radiations is framed as a suggestion.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Apart from the eight extensively reorganized lineages, chromosome fissions are even rarer than chromosome fusions, which are themselves uncommon.
statements.evidence: Outside these lineages, fusions are rare and fissions are rarer still.
statements.note: The abstract states that outside these eight lineages fusions are rare and fissions are rarer still.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Thirty-two ancestral linkage groups, named Merian elements, gave rise to the chromosomes of present-day butterflies and moths.
statements.evidence: show that the chromosomes of extant lepidopterans are derived from 32 ancestral linkage groups, which we term Merian elements
statements.note: The abstract reports that the chromosomes of extant lepidopterans derive from 32 ancestral linkage groups termed Merian elements.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Lepidopteran lineages with extensively rearranged chromosomes have produced more species than lineages that kept the ancestral chromosome set.
statements.evidence: Against this stable background, eight lineages have undergone extensive reorganization either through numerous fissions or a combination of fusion and fission events.
statements.note: The abstract identifies eight extensively reorganized lineages but says nothing about their species richness compared with karyotypically stable lineages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The sex-linked element and Merian elements that are small and rich in repeats are frequently the ones taking part in chromosome fusions.
statements.evidence: Fusions often involve small, repeat-rich Merian elements and the sex-linked element.
statements.note: The abstract states that fusions often involve small, repeat-rich Merian elements and the sex-linked element.
